newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Aug 1.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Friday:

* On Thursday, U.S. stocks put in a mixed performance, with investors taking a cautious tack ahead of a potentially market-moving report on U.S. employment in July. The Dow ended down 32.28 points at 8,222.61.

* Minister of Industry and Trade Tungky Ariwibowo said on Thursday that Indonesia was continuing to negotiate with Japan, the European Union and the United States outside the dispute settlement panel of the World Trade Organization (WTO) over its controversial car policy.

* On Thursday, Jakarta stocks ended slightly down due to profit-taking in blue chips, particularly cement stocks and Telkom, brokers said. The Jakarta Composite Index closed down 0.71 points, or 0.10 percent, at 721.27 points.
* On Friday, the rupiah was traded at 2,605.00/15.00 at 0215 GMT against an opening of 2,613.00/23.00.

* Cement stocks following a report in the Indonesian Observer on Friday which quoted the Director General of Metal, Machinery and Basic Chemical Industries Effendi Sudarsono as saying the increasing production capacity from existing and new plants will guarantee increasing supply in the coming years.
Sudarsono was also quoted as saying that government will continue to provide opportunities to investors to built new cement plants.
* Semen Gresik after a company official said that net profits during the year were not encouraging although sales during the first half of 1997 were higher than the same period last year.
* Semen Cibinong following reports of a planned bonus issue.

* Bank International Indonesia on media reports that it raised $140 million (364.11 billion rupiah) by issuing securitised future credit card receivables to international institutional investors in the offshore capital market.
* Property firm Dharmala Intiland on reports that it has secured a US$55 million transferable loan facility from 14 onshore and offshore banks and financial institutions.

* Shipping firm Berlian Laju Tanker after Bisnis Indonesia newspaper quoted its corporate secretary as saying that it will propose a US$100 million rights issue and $300 million assets securitisation to finance expansion.

* Pulp and paper maker Indah Kiat after it was cross-traded in large amounts on Thursday. The huge crossing of Indah Kiat boosted total market turn-over to around 900 billion rupiah on Thursday against a daily average of around 500 billion rupiah, brokers said.
* Bank Niaga as Standard & Poor's placed the bank on negative credit watch after the announcement of its acquisition by the Tirtamas Group.
* Bank Arya following its encouraging debut on Thursday when it closed at 1,150 rupiah, against its offer price of 975 rupiah.
